# Phase directive — «`/context` as a local command» (Epoch 4, viola-0.2.0; the head entry at `afa8699c`)

**WHAT IS AN INPUT, AND WHAT IS NOT.** Of the folder this directive stands in, the ONLY files you read or snap are
this directive and the relay files a later send names. Nothing else under it is read, cited or snapped. A fact the
plan needs and this directive does not state is ASKED of the overseer in the P3 block, never looked up.

The operator is AWAY from this session (he answers through the overseers' dialogs): raise NO question dialog for
him. A fork that is his is written to `{run_dir}/founder-forks.md` (the question, the options in order with each
one's cost, the recommendation marked) and the step stops there, saying so. A technical fork is answered by the
overseer's relay at once. **This phase makes NO live start and reads nothing of the operator's real `~/.claude*`.**
In your chat messages name a compiled screen literal, never print it.

## Facts, measured by the overseer 2026-11-19 — cite them as this directive's

- A bare `claude` on this host is 2.1.328 (`~/.local/share/mise/installs/claude/2.1.328/claude`); this builder runs
  it. The live home's `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` holds a 24-row 2.1.328 stamp (`L1`, 2026-11-19T06:54:18Z,
  made through the rig's `VH` arm under the operator's real home, on his own word for THAT chunk). The pinned
  product that drives this session is the release build of `a59da9da`: it relies on 24 rows and reads only
  2.1.328 verified. A binary built from a tree with a 25th relied row reads that stamp as lacking the row.
- The reading this entry was minted on: `L2` of chunk `2026-11-19-the-2-1-328-recorded-fixture-set` — one start
  on haiku under the rig's private config: `context-transcript: absent` before the send,
  `send-1-reply: not-delivered:no-prompt-submitted`, `context-submitted: no`, then
  `context-transcript-after: read`, `context-tags: 1`, `context-post: tag`. One reading, no verification.
- `SF` of chunk `2026-11-19-a-live-stopfailure-payload` read the hint carry from the first drawn cell past the
  prompt glyph alone (`hint-attr: inverse`, `typed-attr: plain`), which may be the cursor's cell. The rig's kept
  record dir is keyed by the CLI version since that chunk; its `SF` arm runs inside a `bwrap` sandbox and refuses
  `no-runtime-dir` where `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` is unset.
- The documentation leaves hold no figure the code states (counts, member lists, versions): this chunk adds none.

## The directive

1. Scope is the route entry and its carries as they stand at `afa8699c`, nothing wider: `/context` listed among
   the local commands a send confirms by its post-condition, its ledger row and verify probe, stamped live; the
   hint's cell attribute read on every drawn hint cell past the cursor's cell; the intermittent rehearsal red
   (acted on only at its next red). Every carry is disposed by name in the plan.
2. **This is a PRODUCT change with a relied ledger row. The size risk is the RE-STAMP and what it does to the
   running product.** Say at P3, from the code and the earlier chunks' plans and reports in the store (the
   local-command rows and their probes; the re-stamp chunk `2026-11-18-the-live-home-s-re-stamp-and-the-product-re-pin`),
   with NO start:
   - what the new row is exactly (its name, its probe, the post-condition read, what `absent` on it means for a
     version), and whether it is RELIED — so that every binary built after it reads every stamped version
     unverified until that version is re-stamped;
   - what «stamped live» needs: a `viola verify` under which home (a test-owned one, the rig's private config, or
     the operator's real `~/.viola` through `VH`), how many `claude` processes, every byte typed, every file
     written and where; and what stays TRUE of the running pinned product and this builder through it (the
     pinned binary is not rebuilt, replaced or re-pinned by this chunk; a re-pin is its own operator step);
   - whether the first send's `not-delivered:no-prompt-submitted` reply on `/context` is the thing the listing
     mends (a local command confirmed by its post-condition, not by a submitted prompt), and what a send of
     `/context` reads AFTER the change on a version where the tag does not appear;
   - whether one implement window holds it, or the entry splits (the product change and its fake-agent
     rehearsals · the live stamp) and where.
3. **At P3's END, before P4, stop with ONE block in `founder-forks.md`:** your window; the split or no split;
   every live start's SHAPE before the count — processes, every byte typed, the stop, every file written and
   where, and under WHICH home; for each start a predicate its reading can FAIL, the red reading named; what each
   start READS from a payload, a transcript or a screen (key names, a tag's presence or count, cell attributes —
   never a text) and whether any of it is a reading no row yet names (a widening is said as one, here, not at
   P4); whether any typed key moves the wheel before a send; a recommended cap and what one spare would be for;
   the keys the hint reading needs (how many, where, when). The cap, the keys, any read or write under his real
   home and any widening are the founder's.
4. **For every capped start, name what it needs ABSENT or PRESENT on disk outside the tree** (a kept dir, a
   scratch, a stamp file, a runtime dir), and give each a no-start gate entry that reads it right before the
   start, placed so a round resumed at one entry still fires it; a start whose product is kept or stamped gets an
   entry that reads that product AFTER it.
5. One ledger, one count: `--cap` counts the base starts in the ledger FILE. A census entry after the LAST live
   leg is keyed to the operator leg.
6. Every control stands on an entry filtered to its guard's own cases AND building the whole workspace where the
   case needs a root binary; its `--timeout S` named and passed, ids within 16 characters. Every filter term of
   a gate entry SELECTS at least one test under its layer flag. An expect atom must be able to fail; a word that
   may honestly read two ways is a READING recorded, not a failing atom. A test that skips prints its reason,
   and the entry that owns it says how the skip is read.
7. Before a live round the host is read (`hostwatch.py read --last 15`): a CONTENDED reading with a NEIGHBOUR
   named stops and is re-read, never retried into. A start refused for the token window is uncounted — stop and
   say so.
8. No mutation run. A test that waits takes a bound under the 20 s lint. Every TEST start runs under a
   test-owned user home. Read `df` before a step that rebuilds whole.
9. A fold is decided at the PHASE. A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop
   and tell the overseer. On an account-limit refusal, stop where you are.
10. Call NO scheduled-wake or timer tool, with any argument. End every process you start.
11. Run the phase exactly as the letters say. On the P5 card, in one block, verbatim where a tool printed it: the
    union's per-master lines and the `rows-union` line; whether EVERY cited row is in the union or its standing
    list; every `[RETYPED]` line and re-spawn; every non-zero exit, refusal, `UNPARSED` / `INDETERMINATE` /
    `NOT DERIVED` line; every place a letter was wrong or silent.

  `send-confirmed{confirmed:false}`. Proven in `bash scripts/agent-run.sh run --integration --filter 'binary(cli_send) |
  binary(cli_verify)'` (tests · decision/local-command-unconfirmable; `inputs#I2` item 5).

# Implement directive — «`/context` as a local command» (chunk 2026-11-19-context-as-a-local-command)

The plan is approved (P5 card 2). This window is fresh: read the chunk's documents and run dir from disk first. This
directive is the only file of its folder you read or snap.

**In your own chat messages never print a compiled screen literal verbatim**: name it. Files may hold them; a
message row that quotes one refuses the driver's sends.

## The live cap for THIS chunk (the founder's own answers, 2026-11-19T19:50:29Z; nothing widens it)

- **TWO base starts and ONE spare, on one ledger, claude 2.1.328 by path, under the rig's PRIVATE config: `CS`
  first (`--cap 1`), then `CC` (`--cap 2`); the spare is ONE of `CS-2` or `CC-2`.** `CS`: one `viola verify` into
  the rig's SCRATCH viola home — 9 `claude` processes one at a time, only verify's compiled literals typed (Run B's
  eighth paste `/context` among them), no byte into any dialog; its 25-row stamp kept for `CC`. `CC`: one wrapped
  `claude`, a compiled prompt send first, then the `/context` send.
- **The spare is spent only on a start stopped BEFORE its reading** by the host, the token window (uncounted — stop
  and say so) or the rig's own refusal — never to repeat a red reading. A third base start is the founder's.
- **The keys: one `x` and one DEL into the rig's own input box on `CC`, AFTER the second send's reading** — the
  hint's drawn cells past the cursor's cell read as attribute words first; never a text, never a dialog.
- **Nothing is written under the real `~/.claude*` or `~/.viola`.** `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is READ once by
  the rig (a 0600 copy, removed on every exit path); `~/.claude.json` is stamped read-only.
  `~/.viola/ledger/stamps.json` is read for its sha alone, before the round and after each start, and must read
  unmoved. `lacks user-config: unread` is a stopping red. The pinned product is not rebuilt, replaced or re-pinned.
- **The residual of the new paste is MEASURED at `CS` and named in the report** (what the CLI wrote for `/context`
  under the private config, as names and counts, never a text).
- Each start is ledgered with the clock's time (`date -u`) BEFORE it is made.

## The host — another project builds cold on it for hours

- Run nothing heavier than this chunk's own gate entries.
- **STOP BEFORE THE LIVE ROUND, always:** when the code, the rehearsals and the controls are green and the round's
  no-start entries are next, stop and say so in one line — the overseer arranges a quiet window with the
  neighbour and sends the word to go on. Then read `python3
  ~/dev/projects/additional/andromedaV3/andromeda-overseer/docs/tools/hostwatch.py read --last 15` before EACH
  start: a CONTENDED reading that names a NEIGHBOUR makes no start — stop and say so.
- A gate red where no assertion failed on a value (a stall, a timeout, a kill) is read against the same record
  first and never re-run for green into a contended host: say so and wait for the overseer's word.
- Read `df` before any step that rebuilds whole.

## Stops

- **A RED live entry stops implement BEFORE the operator pass** (a RED `CS` leaves `CC` unfired): report the entry
  and what the start itself showed, in its own words, and wait. A `CS` that reads `local-command-context: fail`
  is a reading of the CLI, not a rig fault: nothing is retried.
- **The hint words on `CC` are READINGS:** `unread` with its reason is recorded and the chunk goes on.
- **The recorded fixture sets stay green without a new recording start;** a drift, hygiene or ledger-probe red on
  them stops implement with the suite's own words.
- A guard's or the permission classifier's refusal is never routed around: stop and say so. On an account-limit
  refusal, stop where you are.
- The rig keeps its frames and the kept stamp locally; nothing of the operator's status line or config enters a
  commit. Every TEST start runs under a test-owned user home. No leaf gains a figure the code states.

## On green

Write the chunk report (P4), then run the operator pass in this same window with the `ci.py conclusion` read
(leg=operator) as usual, and land `evidence/operator-pass.md`. Then stop: the wrap is a fresh window's.
Call no scheduled-wake or timer tool. End every process you start.
